description:
We are SESHAT, a six-member team combining design, technology, and scientific curiosity. Inspired by ancient Egypt’s goddess of knowledge and measurement, we’re exploring a bold Marswalk question: what science is still possible when time runs short?

Our proposed interactive map will use NASA mission data to compare science targets, routes, and return-time limits. We value evidence, clear design, and collaboration across GIS, data science, software, and UX. Every Minute Matters.
summary:
On Mars, every minute of exploration is a decision: Where should we go? What should we discover? And when should we turn back?

SESHAT is an interactive, science-driven Mars navigation and mission-planning platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026's "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map."

Using real NASA and USGS terrain and scientific datasets from Jezero Crater, SESHAT transforms traditional mapping into intelligent exploration planning. It helps astronauts evaluate reachable destinations, calculate terrain-aware routes, and balance scientific opportunities against limited mission time.

Explorers can select destinations, approve routes, simulate traverses, and record scientific observations. When new discoveries emerge or mission conditions change, SESHAT reevaluates available options and recommends where to explore next.

Unlike conventional maps, SESHAT connects navigation with adaptive scientific decision-making through a transparent, data-driven prototype.

Our mission is simple: Make every step on Mars meaningful, and every minute count.
details:
SESHAT — Navigate Mars. Discover More.

1. The Challenge: Every Minute Matters on Mars

Imagine being an astronaut exploring Mars. You have limited time, unfamiliar terrain, multiple scientific targets, and a critical decision to make: Which destination is worth exploring, and can you safely complete the journey within your available time?

A traditional map can show where destinations are, but it cannot fully explain which scientific opportunities remain achievable when time is running out or when new discoveries change mission priorities.

This is the problem SESHAT addresses.

2. Our Solution: Beyond Navigation

SESHAT is an interactive, science-driven Martian navigation and mission-planning platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026's "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map."

Inspired by the accessibility of modern navigation applications, SESHAT brings a new dimension to planetary exploration: connecting real Martian terrain, scientific objectives, route feasibility, and adaptive decision-making.

Instead of simply answering "How do I get there?", SESHAT helps explorers answer a more important question:

"Given my remaining time and scientific priorities, where should I go next, and why?"

3. How SESHAT Works

SESHAT provides an interactive exploration workflow built around real data from Jezero Crater, the landing region of NASA's Perseverance rover.

Step 1 — Explore and Select

Users explore an interactive Martian map and select scientifically interesting destinations. The application combines terrain information with geological and scientific context to support exploration planning.

Step 2 — Calculate and Approve

SESHAT evaluates potential routes using terrain elevation, travel costs, distance, and available mission time. Users review the proposed exploration plan before approving their traverse.

Step 3 — Navigate and Observe

After approval, users begin a simulated traverse and follow the active route. Upon reaching a destination, they can record scientific observations and document findings.

Step 4 — Adapt to New Discoveries

Exploration is unpredictable. When a new scientific discovery or mission constraint is introduced, SESHAT reevaluates the remaining exploration opportunities and supports alternative destination recommendations.

Step 5 — Make Every Minute Count

The system estimates reachable destinations within the remaining exploration time, helping users understand the trade-offs between scientific value, travel requirements, and mission constraints.

4. Powered by Real Martian Data

SESHAT uses authentic NASA and USGS planetary resources rather than fictional Martian terrain.

Our scientific foundation includes:

  • NASA/JPL Mars Trek terrain imagery and elevation products.
  • NASA Mars 2020 scientific resources and Perseverance mission observations.
  • USGS geological mapping of Jezero Crater.
  • Martian thermal-inertia data for surface-property context.
  • NASA Mars 2020 environmental observations.

Geospatial datasets are processed into a locally centered Mars Azimuthal Equidistant coordinate system, allowing the application to perform terrain-aware route calculations.

The scientific planning engine uses deterministic graph-based algorithms, including Dijkstra/A*, and precomputed terrain-cost data to evaluate traversal options.

This makes the project's computational decisions reproducible and explainable rather than dependent on unpredictable AI-generated answers.

5. Technology and Development

SESHAT is a browser-based interactive application built using modern web and scientific computing technologies.

Frontend:
Next.js, React, TypeScript, Leaflet, Tailwind CSS, StyleX, and Astryx UI components.

Scientific Processing:
Python, Rasterio, PyProj, NumPy, SciPy, and Pillow.

Routing and Visualization:
Terrain-based graph algorithms, precomputed geospatial data, interactive 2D mapping, and an HTML5 Canvas-based 3D terrain visualization.

Testing:
Automated scientific verification, unit tests, and Playwright end-to-end browser tests.

The final application runs its exploration-planning calculations deterministically without requiring a cloud AI service for runtime decisions.

6. What Makes SESHAT Innovative?

SESHAT's innovation is not simply placing a navigation interface on Mars.

It is connecting navigation with scientific reasoning and changing mission conditions.

Three ideas distinguish our approach:

Science-Aware Navigation:
Destinations are evaluated as scientific opportunities, not merely geographic coordinates.

Adaptive Mission Planning:
When exploration conditions or scientific priorities change, the system can reconsider the existing plan instead of following a fixed route.

Explainable, Time-Aware Decisions:
SESHAT combines terrain-based routing, mission-time constraints, and scientific priorities to make exploration alternatives easier to evaluate.

Together, these capabilities transform a Martian map into an interactive scientific decision-support experience.

7. Benefits and Potential Impact

SESHAT demonstrates how future planetary exploration tools could help astronauts and mission planners:

  • Prioritize valuable scientific observations.
  • Understand terrain-dependent travel requirements.
  • Make better use of limited exploration time.
  • Respond to unexpected discoveries.
  • Compare alternative exploration plans.
  • Document scientific activities and decisions.

Beyond Mars, the underlying approach could inform future research into time-constrained exploration planning for other planetary environments.

8. Current Capabilities and Limitations

The current SESHAT prototype demonstrates interactive mapping, terrain-aware route planning, destination selection, route approval, simulated traversal, scientific observation recording, travel estimation, and mission replanning scenarios.

SESHAT is a research and educational proof-of-concept, not a flight-certified astronaut navigation or safety system. Its estimated travel costs and simulated mission scenarios depend on modeling assumptions and available datasets. They do not establish actual EVA safety, validate all possible terrain hazards, or replace mission-control decisions.

Future development could incorporate additional terrain observations, environmental constraints, and operational validation.

9. Our Vision

Mars exploration is not only about traveling farther. It is about making better scientific decisions with the time and resources available.

SESHAT brings mapping, scientific exploration, and adaptive planning together to demonstrate a more intelligent approach to planetary navigation.

Because on Mars, the question isn't just where we can go.

It's where we should go next.

SESHAT — Make Every Step Count.
